content: Do not take enalapril and hydrochlorothiazide if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately, as it may harm the fetus. The combination of enalapril and hydrochlorothiazide is prescribed to treat high blood pressure. Enalapril belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, which work by reducing certain chemicals that tighten blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more smoothly. Hydrochlorothiazide is a diuretic, or water pill, that helps the kidneys eliminate excess water and salt from the body through urine. This medication is available as a tablet to be taken orally, usually once or twice daily, with or without food. To ensure consistent use, take it at the same time every day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. Enalapril and hydrochlorothiazide help control high blood pressure but do not cure it. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking enalapril and hydrochlorothiazide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to enalapril, hydrochlorothiazide, or any related medications, including other ACE inhibitors or sulfa drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Mention specific medications such as NSAIDs (e.g., aspirin, indomethacin), cholestyramine, colestipol, diuretics, insulin or oral diabetes medications, lithium, oral steroids, other blood pressure medications, pain medications, phenobarbital, and potassium supplements. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had heart, parathyroid, liver, or kidney disease; lupus; diabetes; allergies; asthma; gout; or angioedema (a condition causing hives, difficulty breathing, and swelling of the face, lips, throat, tongue, hands, or feet). Notify your doctor if you are planning to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking this medication. Ask your doctor about the safe use of alcohol while on this medication, as alcohol can worsen its side effects. Be aware that diarrhea, vomiting, dehydration, and excessive sweating can lead to a drop in blood pressure, causing lightheadedness or fainting. Consult your doctor before using potassium-containing salt substitutes. If prescribed a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Enalapril and hydrochlorothiazide may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they persist or worsen: cough, dizziness, headache, excessive tiredness, muscle cramps, or decreased sexual ability. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience lightheadedness, swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; hoarseness; difficulty breathing or swallowing; fever, sore throat, chills, or other signs of infection; yellowing of the skin or eyes; dry mouth; thirst; weakness; infrequent urination; upset stomach; vomiting; fainting; chest pain; or a fast or irregular heartbeat. Report any unusual problems to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the person has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Regular blood pressure checks and lab tests may be necessary to monitor your response to the medication. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
